book.title: The Monk Who Sold His Ferrari
book.author: Robin S. Sharma

confidence_note: The book is a fable; Julian Mantle and John are fictional. Details verified in the full text (ch. 1-5). The old text's 'monastery' is wrong: he lived with the Sages of Sivana in a mountain village; 'years' is about three years by John's account. Julian's earlier 'great tragedy' is hinted at in ch. 1 but not used.
facts: Robin Sharma's book is a fable told by John, a lawyer, about his mentor Julian Mantle, one of the country's most distinguished trial lawyers.
Julian worked eighteen-hour days and owned a mansion, a private jet, a summer home on a tropical island and his prized possession, a shiny red Ferrari parked in the center of his driveway.

He could not sleep more than a couple of hours without waking guilty about a file; his marriage failed and he stopped speaking to his father; at fifty-three he looked as if he were in his late seventies.
On a Monday morning in courtroom number seven, arguing the Air Atlantic case, he collapsed with a massive heart attack in front of a packed room; the bailiff started CPR.
His doctor's ultimatum was the Law or his life. He quit, sold the mansion, the plane, the island and even the Ferrari, and went to India.
A temple caretaker told him of the Great Sages of Sivana somewhere high in the Himalayas; nobody knew where. Julian climbed alone, without a Sherpa guide, and found them.
Within three weeks in Sivana he began noticing beauty in ordinary things like a spider's web after rain.
About three years later, a man who looked to be in his mid-thirties knocked on John's office door and refused to leave until John saw him. It was Julian, his face lineless, his cough gone.
scene_details: the red Ferrari parked in the center of the driveway
courtroom number seven on a Monday morning
tension: The man with everything collapses in the courtroom where he once won his biggest case, and comes back years later unrecognizable.
opening_idea: Open on the collapse in a packed courtroom, the bailiff doing CPR.

lessons.idea: Treat early warning signs in your own life as information, before an outside event forces the decision.
lessons.anchor: Sleepless nights, failed marriage, looking 70s at 53, then the heart attack and the ultimatum.

reflect_final: Which signal from your body or your relationships have you been explaining away because work seemed more urgent?

use_cases.move: In Sharma's fable, Julian had the Ferrari and the jet and still collapsed in court. Ask what their body has been telling them lately.

use_cases.situation: Your manager praises you for always being reachable
use_cases.move: Say you want to agree on hours when you're not reachable, so the work stays good.

use_cases.situation: You notice you wake at night thinking about files
use_cases.move: Write down that sign and one thing you'll drop this week; see how the next nights go.

pocket_idea: Julian sold the Ferrari only after the courtroom collapse; read your warning signs while you can still choose.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: The lawyer who had the red Ferrari had to sell it to find out why he had collapsed.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Julian Mantle, star trial lawyer with a Ferrari and a jet, collapses with a heart attack in court. Doctor: law or life. He sells everything, goes to India, finds the Sages of Sivana, and three years later shows up at John's office looking decades younger.
